hardcoded.text: That is not a G Launcher backup
A backup carries every distro you have set up, not just $name,
Photos are not inside the backup, only the list of them. Restoring onto the same phone finds them again; onto a new one, your collections come back empty and ready to fill.
Folder size, shape and sort order go back to their defaults. The folders themselves and everything in them are untouched.
The apps are not touched. They leave their folders and return to the list, and the folders themselves are removed.
These settings return to the distro defaults. Nothing you made or added is removed.
Rotation, fit and lock. Your photos stay

Every setting on this distro returns to its default, including your folders, desklets and arrangements here, and the settings shared across distros. Other distros keep their own setups. Photos, collections and installed packs are not deleted.
Settings only. Folders, desklets, arrangements and photos stay exactly where they are.

It leaves the collection and this copy is deleted. Your original is not touched, and if it is on screen right now the screen does not change.
The copies in this collection are deleted. Your originals are not touched, and the screen does not change.

Rotation, fit and the lock-screen switch go back to their defaults. Your photos, your collections and the wallpaper on screen right now are untouched.

an app is a leaf. cat it to read it, open it to launch it
try ~ for files or /apps to browse apps
grant one folder once and every file verb works inside it
Every command stays free, and so does one saved server with a password.

Four gesture actions need it: open the notification shade, open quick settings, show recent apps, and lock the screen. Android gives a third-party launcher no other way to do those four things.\n\nEvery other part of G Launcher works without it, including all the other gesture actions.

It does not read what is on your screen. It does not record what you type. It does not watch what you do in other apps. It does not collect, store, or share any data, and it sends nothing anywhere.\n\nG Launcher asks for no accessibility events, watches no packages, and does not request permission to retrieve window content.

Continue opens Android\'s own accessibility settings. That page warns that G Launcher can "observe your actions". Android shows that line for every app that uses this API. It describes what the API can do, not what G Launcher does.\n\nNothing is enabled until you switch it on there, and you can switch it off again at any time in Settings, Accessibility.
